title: Advanced N-Type Ionic Thermoelectric Cells Featuring Bidirectional Cationic Anchoring Strategy and REDOX Electrode

segments.text: The design of high-performance n-type ionic thermoelectric cells (i-TE cells) tailored for harvesting low-grade thermal energy presents significant challenges.

In this study, an n-type i-TE cell exhibiting substantial negative thermopower and a high output energy density is developed by leveraging the synergistic interplay between thermal diffusion within an ionic hydrogel electrolyte and redox reactions at the electrode interface.

Specifically, a gel network featuring dual positive groups is synthesized by cross-linking quaternized chitosan and guanidine molecules via glutaraldehyde, with thermal diffusion further enhanced by incorporating crown ether for complexation.
Additionally, NiCo(CO3)(OH)(2), a material known for its high hydrophilicity, is utilized as the anode to facilitate rapid ion and electron transfer at the electrode interface.

The integration of optimized thermal diffusion within polycationic electrolytes with electrode interface-enhanced ion/electron transport mechanisms significantly improves the sustained output performance and thermoelectric conversion efficiency of the i-TE cell.

Notably, the thermopower (Seebeck coefficient) of this n-type i-TE cell achieves a value of -26.04 mV K-1, and its 2 h output energy density reached 1301.61 J m(-2) under a temperature difference (Delta T) of 15 K.
These findings offer a novel design paradigm for high-performance n-type i-TE cell.

title: Insight into the ionic thermoelectric effect and electrochemical energy storage of Portland cement

segments.text: The porous structure of Portland cement enables free ion diffusion.
This study thoroughly explores its ionic thermoelectric properties, electrochemical energy storage performance, and the underlying mechanisms.

When the pore solution contains high concentrations of OH- ions, these ions migrate toward the colder region under temperature gradients, imparting the cement-based material n-type thermoelectric behavior.
As ion leaching time increases, the material changes from n-type to p-type.

Optimization of pore structure in cement-based composites significantly enhances their ionic thermoelectric performance, with the engineered material demonstrating a Seebeck coefficient of 1.57 mV K- 1 and a power factor of 0.525 mu W m-1 K-2, both of which are higher than those of previously reported cementitious materials.
Moreover, the interconnected porous structure provides sufficient super-macropores and highways for ion storage and transportation.

The solid-state symmetric cement-based supercapacitor shows high energy density of 32.9 mu Wh cm- 2 and areal capacitance of 237.5 mF cm- 2, which can realize stable energy supply for thermal hygrometer.
Modifying the pore structure of cement leads to a dual enhancement in its ionic thermoelectric performance and electrochemical energy storage.
This work overcomes the conventional limitation of single structural functionality in building materials, providing a universal blueprint for developing net-zero energy building systems.

title: High-performance ionic thermoelectric hydrogels via electrohydrodynamic printing for self-powered wearable sensors

segments.text: Ionic thermoelectric hydrogels (i-TEHs) hold great promise for low-grade thermal energy harvesting and self-powered sensing, but their applications are limited by the trade-off between ionic conductivity and the Seebeck coefficient.

A method combining electrohydrodynamic (EHD) printing technology and cyclic freeze-thaw processes was proposed to fabricate a polyvinyl alcohol/sodium carboxymethyl cellulose/sodium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl) imide (PVA/CMC-Na/NaTFSI) i-TEH for self-powered wearable sensors.
I-TEH was constructed with an interpenetrating network of PVA and CMC-Na, using NaTFSI as the mobile ions to promote thermal diffusion.
Ions in i-TEHs were uniformly distributed by EHD printing process, resulting in an ionic conductivity of 34.27 mS cm(-1), which is a 53.5 % increase compared to the traditional methods.

The synergistic effect between ordered ions and Manning counterion condensation effect induced by the electronegative CMC-Na chain improves the selective ion migration capability of i-TEHs, achieving a high Seebeck coefficient of 14.39 mV K-1 (reference temperature of 25-40 degrees C, temperature difference of 10-15 K), which is a 24.6 % increase compared to the traditional method.
The i-TEH-based self-powered sensor exhibits a gauge factor of 2.09 within the strain range of 150-200 % and fast response/recovery time (102/129 ms).
The i-THE-based self-powered flexible sensor can effectively monitor human movements and handwriting recognition.

The synergistic effect of ordered ion arrangement induced by EHD printing and Manning counterion condensation effect provides a feasible strategy for improving the TE performance of i-TEHs, which opens up a new approach for the preparation of self-powered flexible wearable electronic devices based on human body thermal energy.

title: Ionic thermoelectric performance of cement and its modifications

segments.text: Ionic thermoelectric materials integrated into the concrete members of buildings have potential to generate electric energy utilizing thermal gradients.

This paper investigates the effects of nickel foam (NF)-carbon nanotube (CNT) electrodes and the polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogel on the thermoelectric performance of hardened cement and evaluates the use of PVA as a charge carrier between the CNT electrodes and cement.
The porosity of the cement samples was studied using micro-computed tomography.
The results indicate that modifying the cement with PVA hydrogel increases capillary porosity while it reduces the Seebeck coefficient, overall strength, and capacitance.
The increase of porosity observed to decrease the thermoelectric power.

Pure cement samples without any modifications produced significant values up to 28 mV/K for the Seebeck coefficient, which can be explained by the diffusion of water inside the CNT nanochannels and its flow in cement microcracks and capillaries.
These values pave the way for energy-efficient housing with increased grid independence.
